subject: biology
title: The heart and double circulation
key_idea: The heart is an organ that pumps blood around the body in a double circulatory system. The right side pumps blood to the lungs and the left side pumps blood around the rest of the body. Valves keep the blood flowing one way.

blocks.text: Blood passes through the heart twice on each complete circuit of the body. This section covers the two circuits and why they matter.

items.meaning: A system in which the right side of the heart pumps blood to the lungs and the left side pumps blood to the body.

rows: The lungs, where gas exchange takes place

items: Blood passing through the heart twice is pumped again after the lungs. This increases the pressure and flow rate of the blood.
Oxygen and glucose reach the tissues faster, and carbon dioxide is removed faster.
A wall of muscle, the septum, keeps oxygenated and deoxygenated blood from mixing.
An animal with only one ventricle mixes the two kinds of blood, so less oxygen reaches the body.
Right side of the heart: blood to the lungs. Left side: blood to the body.
Blood goes through the heart twice on each full circuit.
The septum stops oxygenated and deoxygenated blood mixing.

blocks.text: The heart has four chambers and is joined to four main blood vessels. Learn where blood goes in and out.

diagram.alt: Tap a part of the heart or a blood vessel to learn its job, then test yourself.
diagram.prompt: Parts of the heart and its blood vessels

parts.name: Right atrium
parts.detail: Receives deoxygenated blood from the body through the vena cava. The pacemaker cells are here.

parts.name: Right ventricle
parts.detail: Pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs through the pulmonary artery.

parts.name: Left atrium
parts.detail: Receives oxygenated blood from the lungs through the pulmonary vein.

parts.name: Left ventricle
parts.detail: Pumps oxygenated blood around the body through the aorta. It has a thicker muscular wall.

parts.name: Vena cava
parts.detail: Brings deoxygenated blood from the body to the right atrium.

parts.name: Pulmonary artery
parts.detail: Carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs.

parts.name: Pulmonary vein
parts.detail: Carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium.

parts.name: Aorta
parts.detail: Carries oxygenated blood from the left ventricle to the body.

parts.name: Valves
parts.detail: Prevent backflow of blood, so it flows one way only.

parts.name: Coronary arteries
parts.detail: Supply the heart muscle with oxygen and glucose.

diagram.prompt: Put the route of the blood in order

items: Deoxygenated blood: vena cava and pulmonary artery. Oxygenated blood: pulmonary vein and aorta.
Atria receive blood. Ventricles pump blood out.
The coronary arteries supply the heart muscle itself.

blocks.text: Each feature of the heart has a job. In the exam, link each feature to what it does.

items: Valves prevent backflow of blood and keep it flowing in one direction.
A leaking valve lets blood flow backwards, so less blood is pumped around the body.
Less oxygen reaches the muscles, so there is less aerobic respiration and less energy released.
Faulty valves can be replaced, using biological or mechanical valves.
The wall of the left ventricle is thicker and more muscular than the wall of the right ventricle.
The left ventricle pumps blood further, around the whole body, at a higher pressure.
The right ventricle only pumps blood to the lungs, so it needs less pressure.
Heart muscle cells have many mitochondria. They release the energy for the muscle to contract.
The natural resting heart rate is controlled by a group of cells in the right atrium. They act as a pacemaker.
An artificial pacemaker is an electrical device. It corrects an irregular heart beat.
Valves prevent backflow.
The left ventricle is thicker because it pumps blood further and at a higher pressure.
Pacemaker cells are in the right atrium.

checks.q: Describe what is meant by a double circulatory system.
checks.a: The right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs. The left ventricle pumps blood around the body.

checks.q: The wall of the left ventricle is much thicker than the wall of the right ventricle. Suggest one reason for this.
checks.a: The left ventricle has to pump blood further, or with a greater force, or at a higher pressure, than the right ventricle.

checks.q: Where in the heart is the pacemaker found, and what is the function of the heart valves?
checks.a: The right atrium. The valves prevent backflow of blood.

worked_example.question:
Sometimes a valve in the heart can start to leak.

Explain why a person with a leaking heart valve has difficulty exercising.
answer_points: Backflow can occur, so some blood flows backwards.
Less blood leaves the heart, or less blood is pumped around the body.
Less oxygen is supplied to the muscles, so there is less aerobic respiration and less energy is released.
Anaerobic respiration takes place, so lactic acid builds up, which causes muscle fatigue.
worked_example.tip: This is a levelled answer. The top level needs both respiration and the effects on exercise.

worked_example.question:
Blood from the body enters the heart through the vena cava.

Describe how this blood flows through the heart and lungs to leave the heart through the aorta.

Include references to the chambers of the heart and the relevant valves in your answer.
answer_points: Blood flows from the vena cava into the right atrium.
Then into the right ventricle, through a valve.
It is pumped into the pulmonary artery, through a valve, to the lungs.
From the lungs it returns to the heart through the pulmonary vein into the left atrium.
Then into the left ventricle, through a valve.
It is pumped into the aorta, through a valve. Valves prevent backflow.
worked_example.tip: This is a levelled answer. The top level needs the flow from right to left through the lungs, including valves, linked to the pulmonary artery and pulmonary vein.

worked_example.question:
The left ventricle has more muscle than the right ventricle.

Explain why.
answer_points: It pumps blood to the body (the right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs).
It needs a bigger pressure, or the blood has to travel further.
Also allowed: a stronger contraction or force.
worked_example.tip: Assume the answer is about the left ventricle if it is not stated. A statement about the right ventricle pumping blood to the lungs is also allowed.
